_comment: Pharmacology-axis flagship seed. Graded, citation-verified Vd / Kᵢ / EC₅₀ / IC₅₀ transcribed from the private evidence run (~/Developer/piru-data/pharmacology-evidence). Each value carries its own confidence (HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW) + a primary-literature reference. fu is left at the default (1) per the Stage-0 resolution; real protein binding lands in the alcohol/benzo verticals. Ingested by ingest_pharmacology_flagship() as peer-review-primary; rows ADD to (never overwrite) existing data and the app resolver prefers the graded value.
name: Ethanol

pk_routes.notes: Vd ~0.7 L/kg (male representative; women ~0.6). Oral F 80–96%, meal/dose-dependent first-pass. Elimination is zero-order (Michaelis–Menten), not first-order — no first-order t½ applies.

True Vdss ~3.4 L/kg (inhaled, IV-anchored); the oral apparent V/F is much larger and route-confounded, so the IV Vdss is used here. Oral F ~6% (inhaled ~18%). 180 min = effect-site/psychoactive duration; terminal plasma t½ (22 h→days from lipid redistribution) must NOT be used for psychoactive modeling.

bindings.notes: CB1 Ki 25.1 ± 5.5 nM (human meta-analytic mean; span 2.9–53 nM). cAMP EC50 5.2 nM, Emax 70% (partial agonist). Active metabolite 11-OH-THC is ~95× higher affinity (Ki 0.37 nM).

pk_routes.notes: Vd ~0.69 L/kg; F ~100% (108% report is AUC artifact). t½ ~5 h healthy non-smoking adult — CYP1A2-dependent (smokers ~3.5 h, OC ~10.7 h).

bindings.notes: A1 Ki ~10.7 µM (human recombinant) to ~61 µM (human PET/CHO); assay-dependent, ~6× disagreement. Non-selective across adenosine subtypes.
A2A Ki ~9.56 µM (human recombinant; single surviving human source). Primary behaviorally-relevant target (wakefulness/arousal). Non-selective across A1/A2A/A2B/A3 (~1.4×).

pk_routes.notes: Benowitz canonical Vss ~2.6 L/kg (range 1.0–4.3). Oral/swallowed F ~40%; inhaled pulmonary absorption near-complete. t½ ~2 h single-phase; cotinine t½ ~16 h; CYP2A6-dependent.

bindings.notes: Activation EC50 ~2.4 µM (high-affinity state). Desensitization IC50 ~9.7–61 nM is 200–1000× lower, so physiological nicotine primarily desensitizes rather than activates. In-vitro, rat-based with human extrapolation.

pk_routes.notes: d-Amphetamine: true Vd ~4 L/kg (oral Vz/F ~5.4 inflated); F ~75% (tertiary, MEDIUM); t½ ~10 h. Applied to racemic Amphetamine as a close approximation (l-isomer t½ slightly longer). XR prolongs Tmax, not t½.

bindings.notes: d-Amph functional release EC50 at DAT 24.8 nM (rat synaptosome, Rothman/Baumann platform). Use ratios within this assay, not absolute (cross-platform 5–25 nM). DA-leaning, near-SERT-sparing.
NET release EC50 7.2 nM (same assay as DAT). NET most potent; NET ≈ DAT ≫ SERT. Use within-assay ratios.
SERT release EC50 1765 nM (same assay). SERT/DAT ratio ~71 — near-SERT-sparing. Use within-assay ratios.

pk_routes.notes: Racemate IV Vss 2.23 L/kg (d-MPH 2.65, l-MPH 1.80). d-MPH oral F 22% (l-MPH 5%); MEDIUM (no DOI source). t½ ~2.5 h (IR); CES1A1 de-esterification. XR prolongs Tmax not t½. (Reference is for the binding IC50s below.)

bindings.notes: Human DAT uptake-inhibition IC50 ~60–140 nM (racemic dl-threo-MPH). Pure blocker — does NOT evoke transporter-mediated efflux (mechanistically distinct from amphetamine).
Human NET uptake-inhibition IC50 ~0.10 µM. DAT ≈ NET ≫ SERT.
SERT IC50 ~100 µM — ~1000× weaker than DAT/NET; effectively SERT-sparing.

pk_routes.notes: True IV Vss ~3.97 L/kg (277 L ÷ 70 kg; Hasler n=3). Oral F 52.7% (n=3, single source, LOW). Oral t½ ~2 h. ~80% of circulating psilocin is glucuronide. Psilocin is the active metabolite of psilocybin.

bindings.notes: 5-HT2A Ki 41.1 nM (human cloned, HEK293); functional EC50 ≤74.5 nM. ~10× lower affinity than LSD. Bidirectional cross-tolerance with LSD (human controlled).

pk_routes.notes: Primary elimination t½ ~3.8 h (2.4–7.3 h at 100 µg); biphasic at higher dose. No Vd record in the evidence run. Long apparent effect duration vs plasma t½ is slow 5-HT2A dissociation (ECL2 'lid'), not PK.

bindings.notes: 5-HT2A Ki 4 nM (binding + crystal structure); functional EC50 261 nM, Emax 28% (partial). Exceptionally slow dissociation. ~10× tighter binding than psilocin.

pk_routes.notes: Vd 1–4.7 L/kg (FDA label, parenteral); 3.5 = midpoint. Oral F ~22–24% (extensive first-pass glucuronidation). Dominant terminal t½ ~2 h; the ~15 h slow phase is a trivial fraction and not for one-compartment modeling. Active metabolite M6G is a potent MOR agonist.

bindings.notes: MOR Ki ~1.2–74 nM across assays (37 ≈ geometric-mean of range). Full agonist in intact-cell functional assays (Emax 96%).

pk_routes.notes: FDA Roxicodone IV Vss 2.6 L/kg; oral F ~60–87% (higher than morphine, less first-pass). IR t½ ~3.5 h. CYP3A4→noroxycodone (major), CYP2D6→oxymorphone (minor, high µ-affinity). (Reference is for the MOR Ki below.)

bindings.notes: MOR Ki ~26–780 nM (~10–22× weaker than morphine; rank order consistent). Full agonist in intact-cell assays (Emax 90%).

pk_routes.notes: Vd ~1.1 L/kg young adults (rises to ~1.7 in elderly). Oral F ~94%. t½ ~46 h; active metabolite desmethyldiazepam t½ ~71–100 h extends duration. CYP2C19 + CYP3A4 (poor 2C19 metabolizers ↑ exposure).

bindings.notes: BZ-site Kd ~3 nM (rat brain); cold-diazepam Ki ~4.8–15 nM across α1/2/3/5 (non-selective classical profile).

pk_routes.notes: Vd ~0.8 L/kg (IV ~0.72). Oral F ~90%. t½ ~11.2 h (FDA IR mean). Metabolites pharmacologically minor (≈single-parent kinetics, unlike diazepam). CYP3A4 only — not CYP2C19. (Reference is for the binding Kd below.)

bindings.notes: BZ-site Kd ~4.6 nM (rat brain); slightly more potent than diazepam. Ashton diazepam-equivalent ~0.5 mg ≡ 10 mg diazepam.

pk_routes.notes: Apparent V/F ~6.5 L/kg (453 L ÷ 70 kg; oral, true Vd likely lower). Racemic oral t½ ~8.7 h (R ~11–14 h, S ~4–5 h). Non-linear PK from CYP2D6 autoinhibition → t½ rises with dose. Absolute oral F is definitionally underivable (no human IV arm).

bindings.notes: Human SERT release EC50 ~1.69 µM (HEK293); rat synaptosome ~74 nM — ~23× cross-platform disagreement, use within-assay ratios. MDMA is 5-HT-leaning (SERT most potent in the synaptosome platform).
NET release EC50 77.4 nM (rat synaptosome, Rothman/Baumann review). Use within-assay ratios.
Human DAT release EC50 ~22 µM (HEK293); rat synaptosome ~142–278 nM — ~80× disagreement. MDMA is DA-weak relative to SERT/NET. Use within-assay ratios.
Weak, low-affinity 5-HT2A ligand (~7.8 µM); not a meaningful direct agonist at therapeutic concentrations. Primary serotonergic action is SERT-mediated release.

_comment: RC-EXPANSION BATCH (2026-06-23 ingestion). Graded, citation-verified transporter release/uptake + binding + human PK transcribed from the private RC evidence runs (cathinones-releasers, cathinones-pyrovalerones, amphetamine-analogues, tramadol-odsmt, gabapentinoids, neuro-eugeroics). The per-substance MECHANISM FLAG is encoded by the binding action: releasingAgent (substrate efflux, EC50) vs reuptakeInhibitor (pure blocker, IC50) — the single most important correction (an α-alkyl or N-ethyl substituent flips DAT substrate→blocker; pyrrolidinophenones are pure blockers, naphyrone the SERT-blocking exception). Transporter potencies are mostly rat-synaptosome — use WITHIN-ASSAY DAT:SERT ratios, never absolute cross-platform nM (~20–150× gaps). Human PK ships only where a controlled study exists; absolute oral F is omitted where no IV arm exists (definitionally underivable). Four transcription-wrong PMIDs flagged in the evidence run are corrected here (Baumann 23072836 not 23303048; Kolanos 24116392 not 24216377; Eshleman 27799294 not 27758844; Rickli 25624004 not 25548109).
name: Mephedrone

pk_routes.notes: Papaseit 2016 (controlled oral): 200 mg Tmax 1.25 h, elimination t½ ~2.15 h; 150 mg Cmax 122.6 ng/mL at ~1 h. Rapid absorption + short half-life — the short t½ (NOT the mechanism) drives compulsive redosing. Absolute oral F underivable (no human IV arm).

bindings.notes: Baumann 2012, rat brain synaptosome release. Same-assay triple DAT 49.1 / NET 62.7 / SERT 118.3 nM → DAT:SERT 2.41 (balanced, MDMA-like empathogen — NOT catecholamine-skewed like 3-MMC). Mechanism: substrate-type releaser (also inhibits uptake), not a pure blocker. Use within-assay ratios.
Baumann 2012, rat synaptosome — same-assay with DAT 49.1 / SERT 118.3.
Baumann 2012, rat synaptosome. DAT:SERT 2.41 — balanced nonselective releaser.

pk_routes.notes: Poyatos 2023 (controlled oral 200 mg): Cmax ~604 ng/mL, Tmax 2 h, elimination t½ ~6.4 h. Earlier onset/offset than MDMA; sustained HR rise to ~10 h. Absolute oral F underivable (no IV arm).

bindings.notes: Baumann 2012, rat synaptosome release. Same-assay triple DAT 133 / NET 152.3 / SERT 242.1 nM → DAT:SERT 1.82 (balanced/empathogen-like, MDMA-like but less potent at all three). Substrate-type releaser, not a pure blocker. Use within-assay ratios.
Baumann 2012, rat synaptosome — same-assay with DAT 133 / SERT 242.1.
Baumann 2012, rat synaptosome. DAT:SERT 1.82 — balanced nonselective releaser.

Chojnacki 2023, rat synaptosome release. Same-assay triple DAT 91 / NET 99 / SERT 169 nM → DAT:SERT ~1.9 (balanced, mephedrone-like). Uptake-inhibition IC50 separately DAT 1014 / NET 559 / SERT 542 nM. NOTE: clephedrone = 4-CMC, clophedrone = 3-CMC — isomer-specific, never collapse the ortho/meta/para axis. Use within-assay ratios.
Chojnacki 2023, rat synaptosome — same-assay with DAT 91 / SERT 169.
Chojnacki 2023, rat synaptosome. DAT:SERT ~1.9 — balanced nonselective releaser.

Walther 2019, rat synaptosome release (same-assay DAT 28 / NET 27 / SERT 268 nM → DAT:SERT 9.6); Blough 2019 same-assay DAT 70.6 / SERT 292 → DAT:SERT 4.1. Catecholamine-LEANING (DAT:SERT 4–10) — MORE dopaminergic / less serotonergic than its para-isomer mephedrone (4-MMC, DAT:SERT 2.4 same assay), the lone DAT>SERT exception. Substrate-type releaser that also inhibits uptake. Use within-assay ratios.
Walther 2019, rat synaptosome — same-assay with DAT 28 / SERT 268.
Walther 2019, rat synaptosome. DAT:SERT ~9.6 — catecholamine-selective; NOT interchangeable with 4-MMC.

Walther 2019, rat synaptosome release. Same-assay triple DAT 80 / NET 53 / SERT 490 nM, rank NET > DAT >> SERT → DAT:SERT ~6 (catecholamine-favouring, NOT a balanced empathogen). FAR more DAT-selective than 4-MMC — a positional-isomer effect, NOT 'ortho mephedrone'. Use within-assay ratios.
Walther 2019, rat synaptosome — same-assay with DAT 80 / SERT 490.
Walther 2019, rat synaptosome. DAT:SERT ~6 — DAT-selective.

Baumann 2013, rat brain synaptosome uptake IC50 (NOT release — MDPV is a PURE cocaine-like reuptake BLOCKER, monensin-confirmed, no transporter-mediated efflux; the bulky pyrrolidine sterically prevents translocation). ~50× cocaine at DAT. Human-HEK ~10 nM (Simmler) / 30 nM (Kolaczynska). Same-assay triple DAT 4.1 / NET 26 / SERT 3349 → SERT-sparing (DAT:SERT ~817). NOT a releaser/super-amphetamine. PMID corrected (23072836, not the gathered-wrong 23303048).
Baumann 2013, rat synaptosome (~10× cocaine at NET); human-HEK ~50–80 nM. Same-assay with DAT 4.1 / SERT 3349.
Baumann 2013, rat synaptosome — SERT-sparing (low-µM); the mechanistic basis of MDPV's cocaine-like, non-entactogen profile. DAT:SERT ~817.

Marusich 2014, rat synaptosome uptake IC50 (Kolanos 17.5). PURE cocaine-like reuptake blocker, no efflux. Human-HEK hDAT ~390 nM. BALANCED DAT+NET blocker (DAT 12.8 ≈ NET 14.2, within ~2–3×), slightly NET-favouring at human transporters. SERT-sparing: hDAT/hSERT selectivity 2893 (Eshleman, PMID 27799294) — the most DAT-selective pyrrolidinophenone. 'Flakka excited-delirium/cannibal' is laundered newspaper folklore, not a distinct drug effect.
Marusich 2014, rat synaptosome; human-HEK hNET ~160 nM (NET-favouring in the human assay). Balanced with DAT, not a dopamine-selective drug.
Effectively inactive — no significant [3H]5-HT uptake inhibition at 10 µM (rat). SERT-sparing; α-PVP's selectivity is over SERT (DAT:SERT ~2893), NOT over NET.
Kolaczynska 2021, human-HEK uptake IC50. Pure DAT/NET reuptake blocker (not a substrate/releaser). Same-assay DAT 60 / NET 60 / SERT >245000 nM — SERT-sparing.
Kolaczynska 2021, human-HEK — DAT ≈ NET; SERT effectively inactive (>245 µM).

Baarset 2025 — DAT IC50 ~13.4 nM from a single proprietary-dye assay (LOW; NOT the Kolaczynska panel). Potency ~equivalent to α-PVP at DAT, slightly lower at NET, SERT-sparing (DAT>>NET>SERT). Ship rank/mechanism, not the absolute number as fact: pure pyrrolidinophenone reuptake blocker, distinct chain isomer of α-PHP.

Rickli 2015, human-HEK uptake IC50. Naphyrone is the pyrovalerone-family OUTLIER: a NON-selective triple reuptake inhibitor (DAT 40 / NET 11.7 / SERT 46 nM) — the ONLY pyrovalerone that potently blocks SERT, so it is NOT SERT-sparing and carries serotonergic-interaction relevance the rest of the family lack. Pure blocker, no efflux.
Rickli 2015, human-HEK — most potent of the triple. Same-assay with DAT 40 / SERT 46.
Rickli 2015, human-HEK. Potent SERT block (~46 nM) — the family exception; do NOT mark naphyrone SERT-sparing.

Kolaczynska 2021, human-HEK uptake IC50. Pure DAT/NET reuptake blocker, DAT-preferring, SERT-sparing. Same-assay DAT 70 / NET 140 / SERT 11000 nM (DAT:SERT ~157). DAT potency tracks side-chain length: MDPV 30 > MDPBP 70 > MDPPP 540 nM (a real SAR ladder, not uniform class potency).
Kolaczynska 2021, human-HEK — same-assay with DAT 70 / SERT 11000.
Kolaczynska 2021, human-HEK — SERT-sparing (DAT:SERT ~157).

Kolaczynska 2021, human-HEK uptake IC50. Pure DAT/NET reuptake blocker — the LEAST potent pyrrolidinophenone (family floor), DAT-preferring, SERT-sparing. Same-assay DAT 540 / NET 1700 / SERT 43000 nM (DAT:SERT ~80).
Kolaczynska 2021, human-HEK — same-assay with DAT 540 / SERT 43000.
Kolaczynska 2021, human-HEK — SERT-sparing.

Wee 2005, rat synaptosome release (PAL-353). Same-assay triple DA 24.2 / NE 16.1 / 5-HT 1937 nM → ~80× DA-over-5HT selectivity, strongly catecholamine-selective (≈plain amphetamine). Substrate-type releaser. The serotonergic lean is a PARA property (4-FA/4-MA) — do NOT propagate to 3-FA. The forum '2-FA ~24 nM' figure is actually THIS meta isomer. Use within-assay ratios.
Wee 2005, rat synaptosome — most potent of the triple (NE 16.1 < DA 24.2 << 5-HT 1937).
Wee 2005, rat synaptosome — the LEAST potent 5-HT releaser of the series; catecholamine-selective.

pk_routes.notes: Toennes 2019 (CONTROLLED oral 100 mg): t½ ~8–9 h (enantioselective, R-isomer longer), Tmax ~2 h, Cmax median 195 ng/mL — the fluoroamphetamine family's ONLY human PK. Absolute oral F underivable (no IV arm). NOTE: 4-FA carries a disproportionate severe-toxicity signal (cerebral hemorrhage, reverse-Takotsubo, MI, fatalities) with BP effects EXAGGERATED vs MDMA — NOT a safer 'ecstasy-light'.

bindings.notes: Wee 2005, rat synaptosome release (PAL-303). Same-assay triple DA 51.5 / NE 28.0 / 5-HT 939 nM. Substrate-type releaser with concurrent uptake inhibition; more serotonergic than the meta/ortho fluoro isomers (a para-position property). Use within-assay ratios.
Wee 2005, rat synaptosome — same-assay with DA 51.5 / 5-HT 939.
Wee 2005, rat synaptosome — para-position serotonergic lean (vs 3-FA's 1937 nM).

Wee 2005, rat synaptosome release. Same-assay triple SERT 53.4 / NET 22.2 / DAT 44.1 nM — near-BALANCED, STRONGLY serotonergic relative to the fluoro isomers (in vivo 5-HT ~18× baseline >> DA ~5×). The most potent 5-HT releaser of the series. PMA-like dual mechanism behind >12 European fatalities. Use within-assay ratios.
Wee 2005, rat synaptosome — same-assay with SERT 53.4 / DAT 44.1.
Wee 2005, rat synaptosome — balanced DA+NE+5-HT releaser.

Ross 1977 — 4-MA is a genuine MAO-A inhibitor (qualitative 'potent'; NO clean modern human/in-vitro IC50 exists). This PMA-like dual mechanism (serotonin-releaser + MAO-A inhibition) is the serotonin-toxicity / hyperthermia danger and is RING-POSITION-SPECIFIC to 4-MA (para-methyl) — never propagate it to the fluoro isomers. NEVER ship 4-MTA's ~250 nM here (4-MTA is a different compound, 4-methylTHIOamphetamine).

pk_routes.reference: FDA ULTRAM (tramadol HCl) Prescribing Information, NDA 20-281
pk_routes.notes: FDA ULTRAM PI: racemic t½ 6.3 ± 1.4 h, Vd ~2.7 L/kg, ~20% protein-bound. Oral F ~68–75% single dose, rising toward ~90–100% with REPEATED dosing (saturable first-pass: steady-state Cmax +16%, AUC +36%). Parent tramadol is itself an active SNRI (monoaminergic + seizure-threshold-lowering); only the µ-OPIOID limb is CYP2D6/M1-gated.

bindings.notes: Gillen 2000 (CHO) racemic µ-OR Ki 2400 nM; Raffa 1996 (HN9.10) 17000 nM — weak parent affinity. The µ-opioid analgesia is carried almost entirely by the active metabolite (+)-M1/O-DSMT (3.4 nM), so a CYP2D6 poor-metabolizer loses opioid analgesia but RETAINS (and may elevate) the serotonergic/seizure liability — tramadol is NOT a 'clean prodrug'.

Gillen 2000, cloned human µ-OR: (+)-M1 Ki 3.4 nM, (−)-M1 240 nM. M1 is the active opioid metabolite of tramadol and essentially the SOLE carrier of its µ-opioid analgesia (~700× the racemic parent's affinity). A potent full µ-agonist with real respiratory-depression risk — 'cleaner than tramadol' is NOT 'safer': there is NO human PK for ingested O-DSMT, so exogenous dosing is uncalibrated (Vd/CL/F/equivalence ship as NONE).

Gee 1996 — the SOLE molecular target: gabapentin binds the Caᵥ α2δ-1 (CACNA2D1) auxiliary subunit (Kd ~59 nM / IC50 ~140 nM), genetically proven causal by the R217A knock-in. MYTH-BUST: NO binding or agonist activity at GABA-A / GABA-B / benzodiazepine receptors and no effect on GABA uptake (clean 38-target panel) — it is NOT a GABA-mimetic despite the name. Any GABA-system effects are indirect/downstream.
Patel & Dickenson 2016 — secondary binding to the α2δ-2 (CACNA2D2) subunit; non-subtype-selective between α2δ-1 and α2δ-2.

Li 2011 — α2δ-1 binding ~80 nM. The 'pregabalin is settled-tighter than gabapentin (~32 nM)' claim is REJECTED: rank order is assay-dependent (displacement 80 vs 140 nM one way; SAR series ~180 vs ~120 nM the other) and the ~32 nM figure has no resolvable citation. What IS robust is pregabalin's higher in-vivo potency and its dose-LINEAR absorption (~90% F, dose-independent), not a binding-affinity advantage. MYTH-BUST: no GABA-A/B/BZD activity — not a GABA mimetic.
Li 2011 — binds α2δ-1 and α2δ-2 (non-subtype-selective); no α2δ-3/-4.

pk_routes.notes: Terminal t½ ~60–80 h (Namenda FDA label; renal-impairment tail to ~100–124 h). pH-DEPENDENT renal excretion (Freudenthaler 1998): ~48% excreted unchanged; renal clearance acidic urine ~210–219 vs alkaline ~19–31 mL/min (7–10×) — urinary alkalinization (diet, carbonic-anhydrase inhibitors) reduces clearance ~80% and raises levels. Oral F ~100% (well absorbed).

bindings.notes: Parsons 2000 — uncompetitive, voltage-dependent, FAST-off-rate OPEN-CHANNEL blocker, IC50 ~1 µM (0.46–3 µM; 0.46 at NR1a/2B). This MODERATE/LOW affinity + fast kinetics is exactly why memantine is clinically tolerated where high-affinity blockers (ketamine/PCP) are psychotomimetic. The circulating '~22 nM' (Xia 2010) is a different extrasynaptic-preferential FUNCTIONAL endpoint, not the channel-block IC50.

Aracava 2005 — α7 IC50 0.34 µM in RAT (−60 mV). SPECIES CAVEAT: human α7 IC50 (~5 µM) OVERLAPS NMDA potency — the dramatic 'more potent at α7 than NMDA' rank order is a rat artifact, NOT a human truth. No human PET/occupancy data.
Rammes 2001 — non-competitive 5-HT3 antagonist IC50 ~2.2 µM (human recombinant). Off-target.
Peeters 2004 — sigma-1 binding Ki ~2.6 µM. Off-target; binding-only (functional direction not established here).

Loland 2012 — modafinil's real mechanism is an ATYPICAL DAT reuptake inhibitor that stabilises an inward-facing transporter conformation (wake-promoting psychostimulant in mechanism). MYTH-BUST: it has NO NMDA open-channel block, 5-HT3, α7 or sigma-1 profile and does NOT share memantine's mechanism. 'Not a stimulant' is a regulatory/marketing distinction (low abuse liability, atypical kinetics), not a non-dopaminergic mechanism.
Armodafinil = R-(−)-enantiomer of modafinil (~3× the S-enantiomer's DAT affinity), same atypical-DAT-inhibitor mechanism in kind. NOT an NMDA/sigma-1 'neuro-nootropic'.
